sources.entry: pypiserver - A minimal PyPI server for uploading and installing packages with pip.

summary.one_liner: pypiserver is a minimal, PyPI-compatible package index server that serves packages from plain directories so pip and other tools can install and upload to it.
summary.what_it_does: It serves Python wheels, bdists, eggs and their PGP signatures from one or more local directories, scanning them recursively and skipping dot-prefixed files and folders. Packages can be uploaded with pip, setuptools, twine, pypi-uploader, or simply copied with scp. It implements the PyPI interfaces needed for pip and easy_install to install and search packages, and redirects requests for packages it lacks to pypi.org by default (configurable or disable-able). Authentication is optional and can use an Apache htpasswd file (via passlib) or a custom Python callable through the API. The "update" subcommand checks served packages against pypi.org and prints or executes pip commands to update them. It is built on bottle and can run under several WSGI servers, selected with --server, or be embedded via pypiserver.app().
use_cases: host a private internal Python package index
upload and install private wheels with pip
mirror and update selected public packages locally
run a PyPI-compatible index behind nginx or Apache
serve packages to MicroPython upip devices
run a small package server in Docker
how_to_run: mkdir ~/packages # Copy packages into this directory.
notable: Minimal PyPI-compatible server that works with pip, easy_install, twine and setuptools uploads
Plain directory storage; packages can simply be copied in with scp
Built-in update command that reports or runs pip commands to upgrade served packages
Directory caching via optional watchdog dependency for thousands of packages
Custom health endpoint and URL prefix support for reverse-proxy deployments
caveats: Does not implement the full PyPI API; only enough for easy_install, pip install and search; documentation uploads are accepted but not saved
Legacy Python versions are untested; pypiserver 1.x is the legacy line without bugfixes
Upload protection depends on configuration; uploads are unauthenticated unless -P and -a are set
keywords: share python wheels with my team
